cases.name: Mixed outcomes
cases.criterion: One success, one terminal nonapplication and one unresolved item stay distinct; no all-success statement.

cases.name: Envelope acceptance
cases.criterion: Accepted batch without terminal item results is pending, not successful completion.

cases.name: Correlation
cases.criterion: Out-of-order replies map by stable item ID, never array position.

cases.name: Missing result
cases.criterion: A missing item reply remains unresolved; the original selected total and operation reference remain.

cases.name: Eligible retry subset
cases.criterion: Only known retryable unapplied items after their minimum retry time may be resubmitted; successes, permanent failures and unknowns are excluded.

cases.name: Unknown reconciliation
cases.criterion: Unknown items use the original operation reference; lookup does not create new side effects.

cases.name: Task completion
cases.criterion: All items terminal permits task-finished reporting; mixed failure/cancellation is still distinct from all changes succeeding.

cases.name: Empty scope
cases.criterion: No item selected produces no batch call and no invented successful changes.

cases.name: Ambiguous correlation
cases.criterion: Duplicate contradictory or unexpected item identities cannot silently assign an outcome to another intended item.

cases.name: Lost envelope response
cases.criterion: Transport loss alone does not classify every item as unapplied or automatically replay the whole batch.

cases.name: Cancellation scope
cases.criterion: Request cancellation only for eligible unresolved items; receipt is not cancellation completion and already successful items stay successful.

cases.name: Recovery to completion
cases.criterion: After eligible retry and original-operation reconciliation, aggregate output matches actual per-item effects and nothing successful is repeated.

cases.name: Dependency nonexecution
cases.criterion: A blocked dependency result is not shown as success; it cannot be retried while its required predecessor has not succeeded.

limits: One declared non-atomic fixture is not evidence of universal batch semantics.
Dependency logic is limited to declared item prerequisites, not an arbitrary workflow engine.
No generated baseline or human efficacy comparison.
